question: Can successful self-timed MLE programs finish sooner under sharing while yielding less useful output, and can admission improve final search quality under equal resources?
evidence_now: 18812:8executions confirm local work/quality reduction.18819:16executions show strict repeated Denoise rank reversal; posthoc log/step/source checks verify completed-fold counts3-to2 and5-to1 under sharing.18807:32search runs failed original final-quality gate.18845 closed with16wrappers but11valid outputs:4candidate timeouts and1kernel-readiness failure, plus1subsequent execution violating the declared infrastructure-stop rule. New-source rank confirmation did not pass. Not significance, fold-only causal mediation, general incidence or E2E benefit.

sources.title: Understanding GPU Resource Interference One Level Deeper
sources.scope_read: Author-hosted PDF abstract and sections2-5, pages2-6; screenshot requested but tool returned no model-visible image, so no chart-value claim based on visual inspection
sources.overlap: Already characterizes resource-specific GPU interference and limitations of coarse utilization and compute/memory complementarity. Studies H100 and RTX3090. Pairing by task category or low utilization alone is not a new or guaranteed-safe rule.
sources.difference_to_test: Our local evidence is changed statistical work in self-timed generated programs, not a new kernel interference model. Historical host traces cannot identify which GPU subsystem caused the losses. Full paper kernel profiling may cost minutes to hours and is not silently free for300second jobs; no deployment or profiler is initiated.

sources.title: Orion official implementation
sources.scope_read: README Introduction, Hardware Configuration and Example on2026-10-16; not a local reproduction or full code audit
sources.overlap: Priority-aware kernel scheduling already has public code and expects operation profiles. Current README lists RTX3090/H100 with CUDA12.6; paper artifact uses an older dedicated branch.
sources.difference_to_test: Do not claim no practical strong baseline exists. Do not silently upgrade the current task image to satisfy latest-main dependencies. Unknown integration compatibility and per-candidate profiling cost must be recorded, not used to label current cap2 results a comparison against Orion.

sources.title: Concord: A GPU cluster scheduler with enhanced interference profiling and asymmetric job packing
sources.scope_read: Publisher-indexed abstract and introduction; direct open403, full text not inspected
sources.overlap: Describes separate interference impact and sensitivity, placement and sharing incentives. Here asymmetric packing means mixing single/multi-GPU jobs, not our single-GPU pairing experiment.
sources.difference_to_test: A proposal to distinguish the job causing versus suffering interference is not by itself a new idea. Our fixed-program deadline/fold observation is a different local measurement, not evidence against Concord or a reproduced comparison.

sources.title: NVIDIA Multi-Process Service: Architecture
sources.scope_read: Official architecture documentation on cross-context time slicing and MPS concurrency
sources.overlap: Multiple CUDA processes sharing a device do not by themselves establish overlapping GPU kernels. MPS is an existing execution-backend alternative, not a new scheduler.
sources.difference_to_test: 18807/18819 establish container/host-training overlap only. They neither measure kernel overlap nor verify MPS state; do not attribute all slowdown to CUDA context switching or generalize the cap2 result to all sharing backends.18845 is closed; no backend change or system installation is authorized by this analysis. A future backend comparison requires exact-node support and owned-allocation isolation first.

sources.title: Adaptive and Efficient GPU Sharing for High-Accuracy Hyperparameter Tuning (DISC)
sources.scope_read: Author primary SSRN abstract, retrieved through search; full paper not read
sources.overlap: Already adapts GPU time slices using observed accuracy trends, with temporal/spatial memory sharing. Quality-aware GPU allocation is not a new objective.
sources.difference_to_test: Our generated black-box programs supply neither a scheduler-controlled progress/quality interface nor fixed work. This alone does not establish a new method.

sources.title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering? (Malena)
sources.scope_read: Abstract, introduction,4.4 and AppendixD.3 ScienceFlow; not full paper
sources.overlap: Directly studies MLE concurrency and resource-admission alternatives. Main claims depend on backbone strength; ScienceFlow worker/admission point differences were not statistically resolved. Do not claim MLE resource-admission quality effects as an unstudied problem.
sources.difference_to_test: Our fixed-program restart pairs isolate resource-conditioned output changes in a local low-cost regime. They do not refute the harness comparison, reproduce ScienceFlow or establish broad gains.

sources.title: IdleSpec: Exploiting Idle Time via Speculative Planning for LLM Agents
sources.overlap: Speculative planning during tool waits is already proposed. Authors acknowledge additional model computation; MLE evaluation uses one seed.
sources.difference_to_test: Using idle time or equal elapsed time alone is not our novelty or equal total compute. No speculative-planning branch is opened.

sources.title: Semantic-Aware Scheduling for GPU Clusters with Large Language Models (SchedMate)
sources.scope_read: Sections3.1-3.3,4.1,5.3-5.5; recheckedOct16 partial-information fallback and skipped eviction when tracking unavailable
sources.overlap: Uses source/history/log semantics and training-throughput interference monitoring. Reading code or avoiding slowdown is not our novelty.
sources.comparison_needed: A faithful cheap interference-aware/semantic baseline, not just fixed GPU assignment; no claim of beating SchedMate from current data. The paper already treats short jobs and missing progress, with fallback and skipped eviction; our survivor-conditioned terminal-trace gaps are neither a new missing-observation concept nor evidence that SchedMate fails.

sources.title: HyperSched: Dynamic Resource Reallocation for Model Development on a Deadline
sources.overlap: Already optimizes best trained model by a fixed deadline and resource budget. Assumes intermediate progress, checkpoint/restore and common scaling properties; do not claim quality-aware resource allocation as new.
sources.difference_to_test: Opaque generated programs adapt their own work to wall clocks; no scheduler-controlled epoch interface. This distinction alone is not a new algorithm.

sources.title: Prediction-based GPU sharing for distributed training (TensorShare)
sources.scope_read: Primary author-hosted indexed abstract/introduction and footnote only, not full paper
sources.overlap: Predicts sharing-induced completion-time increase and constrains its ratio; footnote includes customized stopping conditions.
sources.difference_to_test: Our successful self-timed outputs show candidate duration can decrease along with quality. This warns against treating runtime-ratio compliance as quality preservation, not a reproduction or refutation of TensorShare.

sources.title: DeepSeek Elastic Compute (DSec)
sources.overlap: Overcommit and isolation of latency-sensitive agent sandboxes already exist, including CPU interference protection and separated CPU/GPU function execution.
sources.difference_to_test: Not a new sandbox-isolation system; our current measurement concerns completed MLE predictions and their learned work, not only latency SLOs.

sources.title: AgBench: Agentic AI Benchmarks for Personal AI Devices
sources.overlap: Already reports concurrency versus success/goodput tradeoffs, including local model context errors and timeout effects.
sources.difference_to_test: The18812/18819 fixed-code replays remove model generation and give valid predictions in every case; quality can change without an execution-error flag. This does not describe18845, which has only11valid outputs. Not claiming concurrency harming success is new.

sources.title: Winning by Peeking: Unenforced Budgets and Test-Set Selection Inflate Short-Budget AutoML Comparisons
sources.overlap: Already reports machine contention reducing trials and changing apparent AutoML comparisons, alongside unenforced budgets and test-selection defects. Contention changing a ranking is not generally new.
sources.difference_to_test: 18812 holds one generated program and its input fixed and observes changed useful work and output, not merely fewer searched configurations. Any subsequent claim still needs decision relevance and equal-cost E2E gains; this distinction is not sufficient novelty.

sources.title: Mosaic: GPU Sharing with Latency Guarantees through Kernel-Level Interference Prediction
sources.overlap: Kernel-level slowdown prediction and admission, including RTX3090 evaluation, already target latency SLOs and best-effort throughput. Do not claim adaptive interference admission is new.
sources.difference_to_test: Our current fixed-program output measurements are not a Mosaic reproduction. Successful self-timed execution duration alone does not identify the amount or quality of work produced.

sources.title: Scheduling Real-time Deep Learning Services as Imprecise Computations
sources.scope_read: arXiv HTML abstract and sectionsI,II-A throughII-E,III introduction; not full evaluation
sources.overlap: Mandatory/optional computation and data-dependent utility scheduling already maximize average output accuracy under deadlines. Quality-aware admission or skipped useful work cannot be claimed as new in general.
sources.difference_to_test: The paper assumes a single non-sharing GPU and explicit non-preemptible stages, timing bounds and intermediate confidence, using DP/EDF and a greedy depth update. Our generated black-box training programs expose neither that stage-control API nor a validated intermediate utility curve; adding phase awareness alone is not new. An implementable beneficial decision remains to be demonstrated, without restoring multifidelity or rewriting program clocks.

sources.title: Scheduling Contract Algorithms on Multiple Processors
sources.overlap: Anytime/contract algorithms and time-quality scheduling are longstanding ideas. Self-timed output-quality tradeoffs are not generally new.
sources.difference_to_test: Would require a practical mechanism exploiting nonstationary generated-program behavior beyond classical resource/time allocation; current results do not establish this.

decision: 18807 and18845 did not pass; no extra search seeds, replacement programs or repeated repairs to rescue either recipe.18819 remains a local completed-fold/ranking mechanism observation, not independently confirmed across new sources. Large measured slowdown may already be detectable by SchedMate-style progress protection; do not claim it is insufficient from our host timing. Actual scores under shared deployment are not wrong labels. Aerial improves with less observed work in18819, so preserving steps/folds is not an automatic quality objective.18859 did not start; fixed-program partner intervention remains unanswered. No new method is established. Do not restore multifidelity, timer rewriting or base training.
